question.problem:
The continuous random variable $X$ has the probability density function $f(x)$ stated below. Given that $\text{E}[X]=\frac{7}{8},$ compute $\text{Var}[X].$ 

$$
f(x)=\{\begin{aligned}\frac{3}{4}, & 0<x<1 \\ \frac{3(x-1)}{{x}^{5}},\, & x\ge 1 \\ 0, & \text{otherwise}\end{aligned}
$$
question.worked_solution:
For a continuous random variable $X$ with probability density function $f(x)$ defined over a set $S,$ we can calculate the variance using the following formula:

$$
\text{Var}[X]=\text{E}[{X}^{2}]-\text{E}[X]^{2}
$$

 

We compute $\text{E}[{X}^{2}],$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{E}[{X}^{2}] & ={\int }_{0}^{\infty }{x}^{2}\cdot f(x)\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{x}^{2}\cdot f(x)\,\text{d}x+{\int }_{1}^{\infty }{x}^{2}\cdot f(x)\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{x}^{2}\cdot \frac{3}{4}\,\text{d}x+{\int }_{1}^{\infty }{x}^{2}\cdot \frac{3(x-1)}{{x}^{5}}\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}\frac{3{x}^{2}}{4}\,\text{d}x+{\int }_{1}^{\infty }\frac{3x-3}{{x}^{3}}\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\frac{{x}^{3}}{4}|}_{0}^{1}+(-\frac{3}{x}+\frac{3}{2{x}^{2}}){|}_{1}^{\infty } \\  & =\frac{1}{4}+3-\frac{3}{2} \\  & =\frac{7}{4}\end{aligned}
$$

 

Therefore, the variance is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{Var}[X] & =\text{E}[{X}^{2}]-\text{E}[X]^{2} \\  & =\frac{7}{4}-{(\frac{7}{8})}^{2} \\  & =\frac{63}{64}.\end{aligned}
$$
